Project Justification: 
 
The earliest Powerplant records of this line date back to 1923. 137 structures are still in 
service from the original installation. Additionally, 64% of the structures on the line date 
to 1930 or earlier. While age is not a determining factor for asset replacement, age is a 
factor when ranking circuits for evaluation. A total refurbishment has not been completed 
on this line in the past. 
 
In the past 5 years this line has had 10 operations: 8 being momentary and 2 being 
lockouts. All but 1 of these events have been attributed to unknown causes. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Refurbishment of this line is necessary to provide reliable service to customers served by 
National Grid.  This overhead line refurbishment program promotes safety and reliability 
by addressing asset condition issues and allowing the transmission lines to meet the 
governing National Electrical Safety Code (NESC) under which they were built by 
replacing deteriorating structures and line components that no longer structurally or 
electrically conform to the NESC.

inspection:

insulators and hardware, adds improved grounding, and targeted replacement of conductor 
and shield wire on the mainline and taps, 
 
Alternative 2 - Line Rebuild: If the conductor fails testing and it is deemed the steel 
structures are too deteriorated to remain in service, the circuit will need to be rebuilt, 
 
Alternative 3 - Smart Fault Detection and Automated Line Switching:  This is an option to 
aid in restoring customers during a lockout but will not prevent customers from 
experiencing momentary interruptions.

Controlled, Motor Operators on Packard - Gardenville 182 115kV circuit on the Packard 
side of the Long Rd Station 209, Station 130, & Youngman Taps. All circuit designations 
are in terms of project C081799 completion. 
 
Project Justification: 
 
Adding a Remote-Controlled, Motor Operator to a field Disconnect (RC-MOD) provides 
the field disconnect, also known as a switch, supervisory control functionality. This gives 
the Transmission Control Center (TCC) the ability to operate a field switch remotely, 
which has the potential to isolate faults and bring back customers quickly. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
RC-MODs will reduce the duration of power outages to our customers.

DER/NWA Alternative: 
 
The Company’s Non-Wires Alternative (NWA) Suitability Criteria considers the 
driver/spending rationale, timeframe, and potential costs to address a system need in 
determining whether that need can practicably be addressed with an NWA.  Based on the 
Company’s evaluation, the need addressed by this project does not satisfy one or more 
element of the Suitability Criteria and will not be evaluated for a potential NWA. 
 
Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA):  
 
Reliability upgrades improve the system's ability to avoid a contingency, reduce the 
exposure to contingency, and/or improve post contingency system capacity. Such benefits 
create more opportunities for renewable energy resources (such as PV and ESS) to export 
power, thereby improving the economics of individual projects. Further, improved 
reliability mitigates the need for load customers to operate backup generation, which is 
typically natural gas or petroleum fueled generation.

Program Name:  
Inspection & Maintenance   
 
Associated Funding Numbers:  None 
 
Description: 
 
The I&M and Elevated Voltage Testing Program is funded annually to inspect and 
address overhead and underground distribution assets in need of repair or replacement.  
This program is mandated under case 04-M-0159 by the New York State Public Service 
Commission (PSC).  
 
Project Justification: 
 
The PSC requirements include: 
 
• Annual elevated voltage testing on all utility facilities capable of conducting 
electricity and that are publicly accessible, including municipal-owned 
streetlights.  Elevated voltage testing shall be performed based on a 1 volt 
standard set by the PSC. 
 
• Inspection program on a five-year cycle that shall include, at a minimum, visual 
examination of towers, poles, guy wires, risers, overhead cables and conductors, 
transformers, breakers, switches, other above ground equipment and facilities, the 
interior of manholes, service boxes, vaults, and other underground structures. 
 
Exhibit___(EIOP-8) 
          Page 1 of 204


--- Page 529 ---
 
Significant Sub-Transmission Capital Investment 
Plan Projects and Programs 
Exhibit_(EIOP-8) 
 
Page 2 of 204 
C026165,C026166 C026167 
I&M - Sub-T Line Work From Insp. 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020 
 
 
• A quality assurance program to ensure timely and proper compliance with safety 
standards. 
 
In addition to meeting the requirements above, the program will drive a consistent 
inspection approach to benefit customers by evaluating asset health and allowing for a 
safe, adequate system.  This program is intended to meet National Electrical Safety Code 
(NESC) section 214 which outlines inspection of equipment guidelines.  Additionally, 
this program will allow for the avoidance of potential environmental issues related to 
some assets, such as transformers. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
The primary driver of the program is public and employee safety.  Asset replacement 
prior to failure provides incremental employee and public safety benefits and avoidance 
of potential environmental problems related to some assets, i.e., transformers and 
capacitor banks.  In addition, implementation of this strategy addresses safety concerns 
relating to contact voltage on all publicly accessible Company distribution and sub-
transmission overhead and underground line facilities. 
 
Asset condition is a secondary driver.  The combination of cyclical inspection and 
replacement of deteriorated equipment provides for a sustainable system while retaining 
assets in service until condition warrants their replacement. 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Alternative 1 - Do nothing and repair or replace assets upon failure.  The I&M and 
Elevated Voltage testing programs are required and employing a fix-on-fail approach is 
not an option.  Furthermore, such an approach would create increased risk of failure of 
assets resulting in a potentially negative impact to public safety and reliability.  
 
DER/NWA Alternative: 
 
The Company’s Non-Wires Alternative (NWA) Suitability Criteria considers the 
driver/spending rationale, timeframe, and potential costs to address a system need in 
determining whether that need can practicably be addressed with an NWA.  Based on the 
Company’s evaluation, the need addressed by this project does not satisfy one or more 
element of the Suitability Criteria and will not be evaluated for a potential NWA.

This project C046439 has a companion Dline transfer project C084566 for 61 poles. 
 
Description: 
 
As detailed in the Alternatives section, two alternatives were considered for this project.  
Alternative 2 was the selected option: Replace 69 deteriorated wood structures using 14 
Chemonite treated wood poles for the woodpecker damaged and adjacent poles and address the 
miscellaneous hardware repairs identified in the Jul 2019 inspection.  
 
Project Justification: 
 
The 27 and 28 34.5 kV lines an integral part of the 34.5kV network in Syracuse and its first 
ring suburbs to the north.  The combined above ground portions of the two lines total 7.3 miles.  
It is constructed with 227 single wood poles and 4 steel towers. Woodard-Ash 27 feeds the 
Galeville Station (1635 customers) and is one of the feeds to the PSC Critical Onondaga 
County WWTP.  Solvay-Ash 28 is the other feed to the WWTP and feeds one customer owned 
substation.  Much of the line has distribution underbuilt and has good access. The lines where 
originally built in the 1920’s.  A July 2019 inspection identifies 61 wood pole structures in 
need of replacement.  The steel towers will be addressed in a separate relocation project due 
poor land rights.   
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Replacing any outdated assets will increase the reliability of the circuit now and in the future.

and 6 spans of conductor, including any "AB Chance 1977-1985 insulators".  Remove the 
de-energized loop to Westmoreland Substation which was previously removed.  Use 
Chemonite treated replacement poles for and adjacent to woodpecker damaged poles.  
 
Project Justification: 
 
Many of the poles and insulators on this line are reaching the end of their useful life.  
There were approximately 69 structures that needed replacement or maintenance due to 
deterioration, increased loadings and woodpecker damage.  On the loop to Westmoreland 
1.34 circuit miles of conductor and 27 wood pole structures will be removed.  There are 
also 5 structures with the potential of needing AB Chance insulators removed.  In one 
area, approval was given to replace structures in danger of washout from area flooding.  
That work was completed in the past using this funding project.  
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Replacing the outdated assets will increase the reliability of the circuit now and in the 
future.

Six Alternatives were considered for this project.  Alternative 5 was the selected option:  
Replace OHGW on 3.5miles of circuit.  Include one OPGW for future communications.  
Repair bent and broken steel members on 6 structures and replace 6 insulator.

Project Justification:

of 3/8" Copperweld OHGW between Station 74 and 78 is an original part of the early 
1900's construction and has failed resulting in outages.  One circuit OHGW will be 
replaced with OPGW for future communications use.  The mile of double circuit 
aluminum sheathed cable is 1950's vintage.  This vintage cable is prone to failure and is 
replaced on a proactive basis.  This Alternative will allow for the coordination of outages 
for the Aerial Cable and OHGW/OPGW replacement.

Description: 
 
Two alternatives were considered for this project.  Alternative 2 was the selected option:  
Refurbishment of 81 Poles and attachments rated 2 or 3 according to the Inspection 
Report(IR). Use Chemonite Poles on woodpecker damaged and adjacent structures. 
Install a switch between Caroga and Royal Mountain. Replace 8.9 miles of #2 and #2/0 
copper wire.   
 
Project Justification: 
 
Background:  The Ephratah-Caroga 23 kV Sub transmission line is located in Fulton 
County New York.  The 9 mile line is constructed with 160 wood pole structures.  The 
ROW is mostly off road with good access.  The line feeds the North Ephratah Substation 
and Royal Mountain Ski Area.  There are a total 2571 customers fed from the line. 
 
According the inspection report, many of the poles and insulators on this line are 
reaching the end of their useful life. There were approximately 81 structures that need 
replacement or maintenance due to deterioration and woodpecker damage.  Operations 
requested a switch between Caroga and Royal Mountain be included for sectionalizing 
the line.  The mainline is mostly #2 copper wire small diameter wire with 188 splices.  
Small diameter wire is routinely replaced during refurbishment to ensure to avoid failure 
when transferring to new structures and safety concern if small wire is not replaced.

Description: 
 
This Project includes the refurbishment of the 6.75 mile line in Ballston NY.  The line

Project Justification:

Customer Benefit:

conductor with 336.4 MCM 18/1 ACSR conductor.  Replace AB Chance vertical post 
insulators (1977 to 1985 vintage).  Improve access and rights as needed to do the work.  
 
Project Justification: 
 
A Number of asset condition problem areas need to be addressed on the line.  
Deteriorated poles and conductor, and difficult access are all problematic on this line. - 
Replace deteriorated assets to improve reliability and met current National Grid 
standards.  Driven by Asset management's goal to provide for the safe, efficient and 
reliable operation of the network.  
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Utilization of part of the walking trail is expected to help the access problem on part of 
the route through the wetlands.

Associated Funding Numbers:  
 
C084726 – Schuylerville Distribution 
C050323 – Schuylerville Sub-Transmission Retirement 
C083967 – Schuylerville Station Retirement 
 
Description: 
 
C084726 – Schuylerville Distribution 
Transfer the Schuylerville station distribution load to a new 13.2kV circuit from the 
nearby Battenkill station.  The new 13.2kV circuit will originate from the existing spare 
R550 switchgear position at Battenkill and will be constructed up to the Schuylerville 
station through re-use of the existing Schuylerville – Battenkill #6 ROW over a distance 
of approximately 2.1 miles.  Also includes conversion of the existing Schuylerville 11 
and 12 feeders to 13.2kV, conversion of 2.6 miles of the Weibel 55, a 1.8 mile extension 
of the Schuylerville 12, a 0.7 mile extension of the Weibel 56, and a 0.7 mile extension of 
the Wilton 51 to produce four new 13.2kV feeder ties.  Additionally, the automation of 
two of the new 13.2kV feeder ties through the utilization of loop schemes is included. 
 
C083967 – Schuylerville Station Retirement 
Remove the entirety of the Schuylerville station equipment and transfer its distribution 
load to the new Battenkill 55 13.2kV distribution circuit. 
 
C050323 – Schuylerville Sub-Transmission Retirement

Significant Sub-Transmission Capital Investment

Exhibit_(EIOP-8) 
 
Page 109 of 204 
C084726, C050323, C083967 
Schuylerville Area Study 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020 
 
 
Remove the entirety of the Schuylerville – Battenkill #6 line and approximately 15.5 
miles of the Schuylerville – Mechanicville #4 line between the Schuylerville station and 
the tap to the Schaghticoke customer owned station.  The Schuylerville – Mechanicville 
#4 line will become a radial feed out of the Mechanicville station.  
 
Project Justification: 
 
The primary drivers for these projects are related to safety, reliability and maintenance 
concerns of the existing equipment at the Schuylerville substation and the two 34.5kV 
lines that serve it.  Between July 16, 2009 and July 16, 2019, the Schuylerville – 
Mechanicville #4 line experienced 48 momentary outages and 20 sustained outages. Of 
these outages, 50 had a cause of "unknown" and 7 had a cause of "device failure”.  A 
2019 inspection of the line found that approximately 90% of the poles on both the 
Schuylerville – Mechanicville #4 and the Schuylerville – Battenkill #6 line required 
replacement spanning a total distance of approximately 16 miles.  Photos depicting some 
of the visible asset condition issues on the 34.5kV lines can be found in Appendix A. 
 
Additionally, a 2019 asset condition review of the Schuylerville station called for 
replacement of the single 34.5/4.8kV 6.25MVA transformer within 5-10 years as well as 
a 34.5kV disconnect switch and PT.  Furthermore, use of a mobile transformer at the site 
is not feasible due to the narrow alley way into the site.  The lack of mobile sub access 
combined with limited feeder tie capabilities at 4.8kV have increased the complexity of 
maintaining the station and raised concerns regarding reliability upon loss of the single 
transformer.  Photos depicting some of the visible asset condition issues at Schuylerville 
can be found in Appendix B. 
 
These projects enable the retirement of the Schuylerville station and the majority of the 
two 34.5kV lines that serve it through the creation of a new Battenkill 55 distribution 
circuit from an existing switchgear position. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Retiring the Schuylerville substation and reserving its load from the new Battenkill 55 
circuit was found to achieve approximately $3M in cost savings over refurbishment of 
the station and serving 34.5kV lines.  The creation of four new 13.2kV feeder ties, two of 
which will be automated, improves the resiliency and reliability of the area distribution 
network.  Additionally, it eliminates the reliability risk of utilizing a single transformer 
which cannot be supported by a mobile transformer due to site access constraints and has 
limited feeder tie capacity.

Alternatives: 
 
Refurbish the two 34.5kV lines by replacing 90% of the poles across the approximately 
16 mile total length and replace the Schuylerville TB1 with a new 34.5/4.8kV 
5/6.25MVA transformer.  Also replace the 34.5kV disconnect switch with a 34.5kV 
recloser and install new 34.5kV PT’s.  This alternative is not recommended due to its 
comparatively high cost and that it does not address the lack of mobile sub access to a 
single transformer station with limited feeder tie capacity. 
 
DER/NWA Alternative:   
 
This project addresses asset condition concerns at the existing Schuylerville station and 
the two 34.5kV lines that serve it and does not increase the overall capacity of the area 
beyond that achieved through the use of standard equipment.  As a result, it does not meet 
the NWA suitability criteria.

the refurbishment of the 7.6 mile line.  Based on historical inspections, it is assumed 30% 
of the structures will need to be replaced. 
 
Project Justification: 
 
Engineering is in the process to identify all concerns of deterioration through field 
inspections and engineering analysis.  It is assumed the 30% of the structure will need 
replacement based on historical inspections.   
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Replacing any outdated assets will increase the reliability of the circuit now and in the 
future.  Interruptions on this line have the potential to affect 5,254 customers.

deteriorated assets that are past their service life.  The 7#8 Copperweld the 7#9 
Copperweld tested at 108% and 122% of rated strength.  The 5/16" steel galvanized 
shield-wire tested at 54% strength.  
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Improving the condition of the line reduces the number of outages due to failures.  Also, 
replacing shield wire reduces the number of outages due to lighting strikes.

8.1 miles of the line that is not relocated.  If the scope of the relocation project shrinks it 
could be bundled with the ACR project.  
 
Description: 
 
Two alternatives were considered for this project.  Alternative 1 was the selected 
option: Relocate 12.9 miles of line to the road as follows:   
• 
Between pole 46 and pole 136 (5 miles).  Build over distribution most of the way 
on Lee, Lovejoy, Stone Church, Haggard, McCormick, English Settlement, 
Scotch Bush and Settlement Roads.  
• 
Between pole 185-258 (1/2 mile, 8 spans).  New ROW required on route 37.  
• 
Between poles 260 and 430.  Build over distribution most of the way on route 
37.     
 
Project Justification: 
 
This alternative improves the asset condition of the line. Additionally, this alternative 
improves the reliability of the line by reducing the number of outages and decreasing the 
time it takes to fix the line when there are outages.

Description: 
 
The Homer Hill – Ceres 809 34.5 kV line is 5.3 miles long including a 1.8 mile tap to the 
North Olean Station 30, and a 2.5 mile tap to a customer owned station at Alcas (Cutco 
Cutlery.)  North Olean Station 30 serves 913 customers.   Two Computapole projects 
were issued for construction that contained several structures along the Alcas Tap and 
North Olean Tap.  Upon issue of the original design, the NYDEC reviewed the work and 
determined that several of the structures and anchors did not meet the current (post 
Hurricane Katrina) US Corps of engineer’s levee standards.   In applying the USACE 
guidelines, the NYDEC is requiring the removal of facilities (poles and anchors) within 
15 feet of the toe of the levee.   The NYDEC provided a list of 11 structures on the North 
Olean Tap and 7 structures on the Alcas Tap that did not meet this criteria  
 
Project Justification: 
 
The project is being done to comply with the NYDEC as well as improve the asset 
condition of the line. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Replacing any outdated assets will increase the reliability of the circuit now and in the 
future. Interruptions on this line have the potential to affect 914 customers.

Program Name: 
 
SubT Line Insulator Replacement program 
 
Associated Funding Numbers:  None 
 
Description: 
 
Systematic replacement of 1977-1984 AB Chance insulators by Division 
 
Project Justification:  
  
Vertical Post insulators manufactured by AB Chance from 1977-1984 have been 
breaking at an ever greater number during the past years on 23kV to 46 kV circuits. It is 
estimated from Plant Accounting records that 2500 structures still have these insulators 
on them. A program is being implemented to replace these insulators as soon as possible.  
  
Customer Benefit:  
  
This program enhances public safety by replacing damaged or deteriorated sub-
transmission overhead line components prior to failure.  Replacing damaged or 
deteriorated components on sub-transmission assets also avoid outages and improves 
customer satisfaction.

Page 159 of 204 
C078518, C078621, C078624 
Sub-T Line Ins Repl Program 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020 
 
 
Alternatives:  
  
Alternative 1: Do Nothing/Defer Program   
Replace the vertical post insulators as damage/failure work when they occur.  This action 
is not recommended on the sub-transmission system because it potentially places the 
public at risk.  In addition, a fault on many of the lines places stress on the other circuits 
in the region and may cause CAIDI and SAIDI reliability indices to increase 
detrimentally.  
  
Alternative 2: Visual I&M   
Rely on the visual I&M Program to detect deteriorated insulators: This action is not 
recommended as the insulator cracking is not easily detected from the ground.  
  
Alternative 3: Replace with Refurbishment Projects  
Replace insulators with other projects where line work is already in progress. In part, this 
work will occur on these type of projects, but not enough work is being undertaken to 
complete all on a ten-year program. In addition, the purpose of other project may not 
adequately address insulator replacement work needed since resources and schedules may 
be given priority, such as for Computapole work.  
  
DER/NWA Alternative:  
  
Since this justification for this project is Asset Replacement in nature, it was determined 
that non-wire alternatives (NWA) does not meet the NWA suitability criteria.

Description: 
 
Replace Cable 11H from Sawyer Station to Station 52, along with targeted sections of 
cables 10, 12, 14 and 15H.  Project is for the replacement of 18,000 circuit feet of cable 
11H from Sawyer Transmission Station to Station 52 with 500 kcmil Cu.  The cables run 
mainly along Kenmore Ave and Elmwood Ave.  The project also provides for the 
replacement of another 15,000 circuit feet of cable to replace portions of the remaining 
length of 11H and the four (4) other cables 10H, 12H, 14H, and15H. 
 
Project Justification: 
 
The project recommends the replacement of 23kV cables from their origination at a 
supply or Terminal Station to the first distribution station.  The cable replacements 
typically take place in groups of four or five cables as they share common conduit banks 
and supply the same distribution stations.  Additional conduits may be required where 
existing conduit banks are full or blocked.

C081704 
Ohio St Duct Bank Interconnection 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020 
 
 
Type: 
 
T SubT D 
 
X 
 
 
 
Spending Rationale: 
Asset Condition 
Communications/ 
Control Systems 
Customer 
Requests/ Public 
Requirements 
DER Electric 
System 
Access 
Damage/ Failure 
  
  
  
  
  
 
Non- 
Infrastructure 
Reliability 
Resiliency 
System 
Capacity 
Multi-Value 
Transmission 
(MVT) 
  
X 
  
  
  
 
 
Program Name:  
N/A 
 
Associated Funding Numbers:  N/A 
 
Description: 
 
The “interconnection” is the missing link from the new Ohio St Station to new UG 
infrastructure going north (MH722).  The city of Buffalo owns a bridge on Ohio Street 
that would serve as a crossing for a portion of the interconnection that cross a major 
railroad yard.  Additional duct in trench would be installed on the North and South ends 
of this bridge crossing. 
 
Project Justification: 
 
The existing infrastructure cannot accommodate additional circuits beyond the two that 
are currently installed.  If one of the existing circuits were to fail in the original 
underground infrastructure, new conductor cannot be pulled in due to asset condition 
(collapsed/obstructed fiber duct). Four-inch fiber duct in good working order is 
physically limited to compact 500 copper at 34.5kV.  Future load is likely to exceed the 
capacity of 500 copper in a congested duct bank. The existing circuits have had several 
faults in the past that were thought to be “self-healing” faults in the PILC cable, as fault 
locators indicated the fault to be in the underground portion, but a fault was never 
positively located.  
 
 
Exhibit___(EIOP-8) 
          Page 176 of 204


--- Page 704 ---
 
Significant Sub-Transmission Capital Investment 
Plan Projects and Programs 
Exhibit_(EIOP-8) 
 
Page 177 of 204 
C081704 
Ohio St Duct Bank Interconnection 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020 
 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
This will allow Operations to replace failed conductors within the aged duct bank.  It will 
also allow for increased conductor size if needed to serve increasing load and additional 
cables to be pulled for future load growth and redundancy. 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Alternative 1:  This alternative would be constructed from a combination of trenchless 
(bore) and traditional duct infrastructure.  The breakdown of each would be dependent on 
engineering/design, easements, permitting and other conflicts that may be encountered.  
We would pursue the solution that has the minimal amount of trenchless infrastructure 
due to cost.  Our current expectation is 1180’ traditional, 320’ trenchless 
 
Alternative 2: Re-use existing aerial cable route.  Would still requires reduced scope 
trenchless and traditional excavation and would require Sub-T engineering to evaluate 
additional circuits on pole, would likely need to change poles.  It would limit future 
growth of additional circuits – may need 5 total and maintains overhead crossing above 
tracks in active rail yard.  Additionally, there is pressure from Municipality and Public to 
reduce overhead infrastructure in this area. 
 
DER/NWA Alternative: 
 
This project lays conduit to provide space to complete the build out of the Ohio St. 
Station. DER/NWA Alternatives cannot meet the need (connecting Ohio St. Station to 
existing UG). 
 
Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA):  
 
Reliability upgrades improve the system's ability to avoid a contingency (hardening, 
flood mitigation), reduce the exposure to contingency (fusing), and/or improve post 
contingency system capacity (MWh violation upgrades). Such benefits create more 
opportunities for DER (such as PV and ESS) to export power, thereby improving the 
economics of individual projects. Further, improved reliability mitigates the need for load 
customers to operate backup generation, which is typically natural gas or petroleum 
fueled generation. 
 
Studies/References:

Program Name: 
10E Cable Replacement  
 
Associated Funding Numbers:  N/A 
 
Description: 
 
Replace Cable 10E in its entirety starting at Elm St Station.  Sections that have recently 
been replaced under damage failure can be further evaluated for need of replacement.  
Scope is high level and estimate is based on raw footage of cable.  
 
Further discussion to develop scope: 
• Would have to be completed in sections, limited by # of “Y” splices and 
connections to vaults/customers.  Possibly 7 separate outages to cable.  Coca Cola 
field is on this cable. 
• Relies on spare conduits along entire run so that cable can be pulled in advance 
and dead sections prespliced 
• Consider 500 kcmil reduced diameter for mainline conductor, possibly just to a 
certain point (third major Y at MH 115 Pearl) 
• Enlist the help of Cable Ops to develop scope 
 
Project Justification: 
 
Replace portion of cable 10E in accordance with strategy developed in 2013.The priority 
list was developed by exporting the cable failure records stored in the NY underground 
cable database into an excel spreadsheet and conducting statistical analysis. The

Customer Benefit:

Alternatives:

DER/NWA Alternative: 
 
The Company’s Non-Wires Alternative (NWA) Suitability Criteria considers the 
driver/spending rationale, timeframe, and potential costs to address a system need in 
determining whether that need can practicably be addressed with an NWA.  Since the 
justification for this project is Asset Condition in nature, it was determined that this 
project will not be evaluated for a potential NWA.

Program Name:  
None 
 
Associated Funding Numbers:  None 
 
Description:  
  
Relocation of structures 237-240 due to creek washout.   
  
Project Justification: 
  
This alternative improves the asset condition of the line. Additionally, this alternative 
improves the reliability of the line by reducing the number of outages and decreasing the 
time it takes to fix the line when there are outages.   
  
Customer Benefit:   
 
Replacing assets in danger of washouts will increase the reliability of the circuit now and 
in the future. Interruptions on this line have the potential to affect 1,390 customers.  
  
 
Alternatives:  
  
In kind replacement is considered infeasible, as it will continue to be prone to wash out.

Description: 
 
The project is a placeholder for future sub transmission automation projects.  As projects 
are identified, individual funding projects will be created. 
 
Project Justification: 
 
Sub transmission automation either limits, or in some cases, eliminate interruptions to 
distribution customers for problems on sub transmission lines. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Automation reduces the number of customers interrupted due to outages on sub 
transmission lines.  This also reduces SAIFI. 
 
Alternatives:  
 
 
None

DER/NWA Alternative: 
 
Since this justification for this project is Resiliency in nature, it was determined that non-
wire alternatives (NWA) does not meet the NWA suitability criteria. 
 
Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA):  
 
Resiliency spends improve the system's ability to re-energize portions of the system post 
contingency. These projects will generally reduce the duration of outages for load and 
generation customers. This means clean generation (such as solar PV) will have increased 
deliverability, increasing the average carbon emissions per MWh in NY with a cleaner, 
more deliverable, supply.

CD00898 
W. MILTON TAP-34.5KV NEW LINE 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020

Program Name:  
Sub-T Overhead Line 
 
Associated Funding Numbers: C048968 - Ballston-Randall-W. Milton 34.5kV rem 
 
Description: 
 
Build a new 34.5 kV line to supply the Knolls Atomic Power Laboratories (KAPL), W. 
Milton station (Naval Facility) from the end of the Rock City Falls 34.5 kV tap 
(approximately 3 miles). Retire and remove the existing 34.5 kV supply line to KAPL 
(Ballston-Randall Road #9 line) using FP C048968. 
 
Project Justification: 
 
Field inspection of the Ballston-Randall Road #9 line has determined that the line needs 
significant repair which would likely require a full re-construction of the entire line. The 
line is 9 miles long and runs through some very difficult terrain with significant 
environmental challenges making it expensive to rebuild. The construction of the new 
Lasher Road substation has allowed all load previously served from the Randall Road 
substation to be permanently transferred to Lasher Road leaving KAPL the sole customer 
being served from this line. The construction of a new 34.5 kV line from the Rock City 
Falls tap to serve KAPL would be about 1/3rd the distance of the existing line and would 
be mostly under-built on new distribution poles being installed along Rock City Road for 
a new 13.2 kV circuit for the Sodeman Road substation.  Construction of both the 13.2 
kV distribution and 34.5 kV sub-transmission circuits will be done concurrently thus 
allowing the cost to be shared between the two projects. In addition, the new line will be 
constructed mostly adjacent to a public road further reducing the cost of installation while 
Exhibit___(EIOP-8) 
          Page 202 of 204


--- Page 730 ---
 
Significant Sub-Transmission Capital Investment 
Plan Projects and Programs 
Exhibit_(EIOP-8) 
 
Page 203 of 204 
CD00898 
W. MILTON TAP-34.5KV NEW LINE 
Version 1 – 
07/22/2020 
 
 
also reducing outage times when the line does experience a failure.  This new line will 
allow for the retirement of the Ballston-Randall Road #9 line. 
 
Customer Benefit: 
 
Replacing the tap to West Milton will provide a reliable 34.5 kV supply to the KAPL 
facility which includes a working nuclear reactor used for training naval personnel. 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Alternative 1 - Rebuild the existing 9 mile Ballston-Randall Road #9 line to KAPL – This 
option was rejected due to difficult access issues including wetlands. Constructing a new 
34.5 kV line from the end of the Rock City Falls tap allows the Company to retire this 9 
mile 34.5 kV line. The full rebuild of this line is expected to cost significantly more than 
constructing the new three mile line. 
 
Alternative 2 - Defer the project – This is not recommended as the existing sub-
transmission line is currently deteriorating which will impact customer reliability due to 
sudden catastrophic structure failures. 
 
DER/NWA Alternative: 
 
The Company’s Non-Wires Alternative (NWA) Suitability Criteria considers the 
driver/spending rationale, timeframe, and potential costs to address a system need in 
determining whether that need can practicably be addressed with an NWA. Based on the 
Company’s evaluation, the need addressed by this project satisfies the Suitability Criteria 
and will be evaluated for a potential NWA.
